items.content_html:
Holistic security for defenders under threat

Holistic security support co-created with defenders and movements at risk, wherever they are.

Open Briefing builds resistance and resilience among the people and movements challenging unaccountable power. We know that working for justice or change can carry real risks, and that asking for help isn’t always easy. We’re here to help you navigate those risks.

Who we support

Open Briefing offers fully-funded holistic security support to a wide range of people and organisations at risk. You might be a defender, activist, or journalist. Or you could be part of a community group, loose collective, or formal NGO. All we ask is that you meet the following criteria:

  1. Purpose-led. Works towards positive social, political, or environmental change.
  2. Community impact. Creates change that extends beyond the individual or organisation to a wider community, movement, or cause.
  3. At risk. Faces a high risk of harm due to activism, advocacy, or public interest work.
  4. Low resource. Lacks access to support due to underfunding or systemic barriers.
  5. Non-violent. Does not use or incite physical violence against people.

You can request support directly below, or ask one of our trusted referral partners to do so on your behalf.

Form not opening? Use direct link 

How we can support you

We offer support across three risk areas:

  • Protection and security: personal safety, home and office security, organisational security, travel security, collective protection, partner security.
  • Digital risk and resilience: information security, device security, account security, network security, secure communications, website security.
  • Wellbeing and collective care: mental health, emotional resilience, staff care and wellbeing, collective wellbeing, ecological belonging, digital wellbeing.

Common ways we might work with you include:

  • Mentoring and coaching
  • Targeted advice
  • Remote accompaniment
  • Training and capacity sharing
  • Counselling
  • Audit and assessment
  • Contingency planning
  • Documentation

We offer our support in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, and Arabic. Additional languages are covered by some teams or through interpreters. Our support is designed for remote delivery, so we can work with you wherever you are in the world. If needed, one of our local consultants or someone from our international team may also be able to work with you in person, even in remote communities.

What is not covered

To remain focused where we can add the most value, our responsive assistance does not cover:

  • Financial assistance
  • Fundraising support
  • Legal support
  • Asylum or resettlement support
  • IT support and troubleshooting
  • Support based on individual identity alone

Due to US law, there are also some restrictions on our counselling provision in some states, though wellbeing coaching is available across the whole country. Please contact us for more information.

Organisations with an annual budget over $1 million USD (or local equivalent) are usually not eligible for funded support through our open programme. But please get in touch – we may still be able to help.

  • Full terms and conditions.

Open Briefing made me feel comfortable and safe at a time when I was the most vulnerable. They worked with me to help identify potential security threats and gave me the tools to better protect myself. The team at Open Briefing provided me with a sense of security, familiarity, and peace. The help they provided allows me to continue advocating for a more just and sustainable world while feeling protected.

Environmental defender, North America

items.content_html:
Risk management for nonprofits and foundations

Consultancy and retained support to help nonprofits and foundations meet their risk management, duty of care, and data protection commitments to staff, grantees, and partners.

Since we have had Open Briefing at our side, our protection work with at-risk winners of the Right Livelihood Award is more effective and proactive. They are helping us enhance our structure, so that we can respond to urgent need. Their team’s expertise, empathy, and knowledge of the situation in many countries makes Open Briefing a trusted partner for us and our laureates.

Right Livelihood Foundation

items.content_html:
Referral network

A community of over 60 partners refer at-risk defenders and organisations to our rapid response mechanism for holistic security support. This includes a wide range of nonprofits, foundations, and protection organisations, including both high-profile and grassroots organisations around the world.

We in turn are a referral partner for Access Now’s Digital Security Helpline, Amnesty Security Lab, and Cloudflare’s Project Galileo.

In 2025, we partnered with ALLIED and KERI to strengthen the mental health and psychosocial support ecosystem for Indigenous, land, and environmental defenders in the Philippines. We also partnered with two regional protection hubs in Southeast Asia – Exile Hub and Tifa Foundation – supporting them through capacity-sharing and mentoring, while learning from their local knowledge and experience.

We are also part of the security working group of the Defenders in Development campaign.

Funding partnerships

We work with funders as a grantee, service provider, and strategic partner.

Foundations trust us to deliver sustained impact alongside responsible stewardship of resources. Current and recent funding partners include Luminate, the National Endowment for Democracy, Packard Foundation, Oak Foundation, Mott Foundation, Equation Campaign, Waterloo Foundation, Christensen Fund, and Bernina Initiative.

As a provider, we support foundations seeking to strengthen protection for at-risk grantees and improve their own approaches to risk management, data protection, and staff care.

Working across these roles gives us a clear view of emerging risks, practical constraints, and what effective protection and philanthropy require. We use that perspective to contribute to more resilient and responsible funding practice.

Alliances and coalitions

Open Briefing is part of a wider ecosystem where collaboration and complementarity matter. We play an active role in civil society networks and multilateral bodies that support defenders and protect civic space, alongside relevant professional associations and private sector initiatives.

Civil society networks

  • CIVICUS
  • Building Responses Together
  • Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders (ALLIED)
  • Vuka!
  • NGO Information Sharing and Analysis Center (NGO-ISAC)
  • Global Mental Health Action Network
  • Mental Health Innovation Network
  • Global Interagency Security Forum (GISF)

Multilateral bodies

  • EU Temporary Relocation Platform (EUTRP)

Private sector initiatives

  • Social Enterprise UK
  • Association of Mental Health Providers
  • Cloudflare – Project Galileo
  • People and Planet First
  • 1% for the Planet

items.content_html:
Tools and guidance for action under pressure

Multilingual tools, guidance, and insights to strengthen the individual and collective safety and resilience of defenders and movements around the world. 

Open Briefing identified key areas of concern and clearly set out the actions that we can take now and in the longer term. Their work went beyond digital security to incorporate travel security and our team’s wellbeing – all through a gender perspective. This really highlights the benefits of their holistic approach.

Women’s Link Worldwide
